reference_document: Perego et al., Using DCAT-AP for research data (SDSVoc 2016)
supersedes: core-requirements.json (v1 rows kept unchanged, marked added_in=v1)
completion_rule: v2 adds every requirement the reference document states for the profile, its metadata or the systems around it that v1 did not contain: a requirement sentence, a rationale, a changed obligation or a reported request. Text copied from DCAT-AP and table entries that only repeat a base obligation without a rationale are not added. Rows that are only proposed, deferred or open issues are kept and marked in status_in_source.
scoring_note: Score level=content rows for need recovery; profile and system rows are reported separately.

requirements.statement: Identify the people who created a dataset.
requirements.source_locator: Metadata elements relevant for scientific data, numbered item 1

requirements.statement: Describe the origin and processing history of data.
requirements.source_locator: Metadata elements relevant for scientific data, numbered item 2

requirements.statement: Give prospective users practical guidance on using a dataset.
requirements.source_locator: Metadata elements relevant for scientific data, numbered item 3

requirements.statement: Connect datasets to associated scientific publications.
requirements.source_locator: Metadata elements relevant for scientific data, numbered item 4

requirements.statement: Identify source datasets used in producing a dataset.
requirements.source_locator: Metadata elements relevant for scientific data, numbered item 5

requirements.statement: Give datasets persistent identifiers, encoded as HTTP URIs where possible, and tell primary identifiers (e.g. DOIs) from alternative ones.
requirements.anchor_quote: For this purpose, it would be desirable to promote the encoding of identifiers as HTTP URIs, whenever possible.

requirements.statement: Express the roles that agents play for a dataset beyond publisher and contact point, consistently across catalogues.
requirements.source_locator: Perego et al. 2016 (SDSVoc paper 27), "Data citation", "Agent roles"
requirements.anchor_quote: A consistent use of agent roles is crucial to enable metadata interoperability.

requirements.statement: Indicate when a distribution gives access through a service or API rather than to the data itself, and which service standard it follows.
requirements.source_locator: Perego et al. 2016 (SDSVoc paper 27), "Modelling service/API-based data access"
requirements.anchor_quote: Denote distributions as pointing to a service / API, and not directly to the actual data.

requirements.statement: Describe provenance in enough detail to support reproducibility and to track how data are used.
requirements.source_locator: Perego et al. 2016 (SDSVoc paper 27), "Additional requirements" (detailed specification of data provenance)
requirements.anchor_quote: The objectives include (a) data reproducibility and (b) ability to track the usage of data

requirements.statement: Describe data quality assessments and include users' feedback on the data.
requirements.source_locator: Perego et al. 2016 (SDSVoc paper 27), "Additional requirements" (modelling and using data quality assessments)
requirements.anchor_quote: it potentially includes the integration of users' feedback as part of the meta/data management life-cycle.

requirements.statement: Publish metadata on the Web so that the data are visible and discoverable through search engines.
requirements.source_locator: Perego et al. 2016 (SDSVoc paper 27), "Additional requirements" (optimising metadata publication on the Web)
requirements.anchor_quote: increasing visibility and discoverability of JRC data on the Web, also via search engines.
